title: FBI Investigating After Man Detonates Incendiary Device Outside NYC Federal Immigration Building
excerpt: A suspect carrying anti-ICE material and a pellet gun is in custody after setting off fireworks and flammable liquid outside 26 Federal Plaza, which houses immigration courts and ICE offices.
body:
• A man detonated an incendiary device outside 26 Federal Plaza in Lower Manhattan on Monday morning, prompting an FBI Joint Terrorism Task Force investigation.
  • The suspect, identified by law enforcement sources as Andrew Arrabaca, was carrying anti-ICE material and a pellet gun.
  • Two people suffered minor injuries; the building, which houses federal immigration courts and ICE offices, was evacuated.
  • The incident comes amid heightened tensions over immigration enforcement, with 26 Federal Plaza serving as a focal point for deportation proceedings.

The FBI's Joint Terrorism Task Force is investigating after a man deployed an incendiary device outside 26 Federal Plaza in Lower Manhattan on Monday morning, targeting a building that houses federal immigration courts, ICE offices, and FBI headquarters in New York.

The incident occurred around 8:30 a.m. when the suspect dumped an unknown liquid on the ground and ignited fireworks on top of it, creating a small fire and explosion outside the Jacob K. Javits Federal Office Building, according to FBI New York Assistant Director James Barnacle Jr.

Suspect in Custody

The suspect was quickly apprehended by Federal Protective Service officers. Video footage from the scene showed uniformed police and agents surrounding the man as smoke billowed from the area. Two law enforcement sources identified the suspect as Andrew Arrabaca to Fox News Digital, noting he was wearing "anti-ICE stuff" during the incident.

https://x.com/NewYorkFBI/status/2079340654648303776

Besides the fireworks and flammable liquid, the man was armed with a pellet gun and had wheeled a cart near the building containing additional items, which the NYPD bomb squad was called in to examine. A federal employee and a civilian suffered minor injuries but were released after receiving medical attention.

"This morning an individual deployed an incendiary device outside of 26 Federal Plaza. The individual has been taken into custody and the FBI New York Joint Terrorism Task Force is investigating the incident."

— FBI Director Kash Patel

A Building at the Center of Immigration Enforcement

The 41-story building at 26 Federal Plaza is far more than a bureaucratic office complex. It houses New York's immigration courts, the ICE field office, the FBI's Joint Terrorism Task Force, and multiple other federal agencies. Located just blocks from City Hall and federal courthouses, it became a hotbed of arrests and detention during the Trump administration's crackdown on illegal immigration.

For the Indian diaspora and other immigrant communities, the building is a familiar landmark — it processes thousands of immigration cases annually and is where many visa and asylum hearings take place.

Political Response

New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani called the incident "deeply disturbing" and said his team was coordinating with the NYPD and federal authorities.

"I'm relieved no one was seriously injured and that a suspect is in custody," Mamdani said. "Our administration will continue to ensure that every New Yorker is safe in their city — and hold accountable any who threaten that."

Authorities have not formally confirmed a motive, though the anti-ICE material found on the suspect points to an immigration enforcement-related grievance. The investigation is ongoing.
